noticias.titulo: Un fugitivo español y el canal NoName057(16), detrás de los ciberataques a web de administraciones y empresas españolas
noticias.resumen: La guerra híbrida es cada día menos invisible y más efectiva. Los ciberataques a administraciones y empresas se ha convertido en un arma potente que busca desestabilizar estados. la empresa tecnológica alicantina Golden Owl acaba de publicar un informe que explica las conexiones prorrusas que hay detrás de algunos de los ataques sufridos en los últimos meses. Los primeros objetivos de la rama española fueron la Universidad de Alicante, el Parlamento Vasco y el transporte valenciano.

noticias.titulo: Rescatan a un hombre secuestrado tras pasar 15 horas atado a una silla y amenazado con un machete en Valencia
noticias.resumen: Un hombre de 54 años ha sido rescatado por la Guardia Civil después de permanecer cerca de 15 horas secuestrado en un chalet aislado de Montserrat, en la comarca de la Ribera Alta, donde fue golpeado, atado a una silla y amenazado de muerte con un machete y otras armas blancas de grandes dimensiones. La operación se ha saldado con la detención de una mujer de 41 años y un hombre de 54, acusados de un presunto delito de detención ilegal, mientras la investigación continúa abierta para localizar a otros posibles implicados y esclarecer las circunstancias del secuestro.

noticias.titulo: Roberta, chef italiana: “Para quitar la acidez de la salsa de tomate, no uses azúcar, sino una pizca de bicarbonato”
Núcleo Nacional "adoctrinó" a menores con el videojuego 'GTA V' para atacar "a otras razas"
noticias.resumen: Los cabecillas de la asociación neonazi Núcleo Nacional se valieron de vídeos del videojuego 'Grand Theft Auto V', conocido por su abreviación “GTA V” para captar y adoctrinar a jóvenes y menores de edad en la violencia y el odio racial, según indica un informe de 8 de julio de la Brigada de Información de la Policía Nacional de Gijón enviado a la jueza del caso, y al que ha tenido acceso esta redacción.

noticias.titulo: Implantes cerebrales permiten a pacientes con ELA volver a hablar y cantar
noticias.resumen: Un hombre que había perdido la voz por la esclerosis lateral amiotrófica (ELA) ha conseguido comunicarse mediante habla sintetizada a partir de su actividad cerebral. Una cantante con la misma enfermedad ha logrado cantar una escala musical. Ambos avances prolongan las investigaciones previas sobre los primeros implantes cerebrales que transformaban señales neuronales. Ahora el objetivo es recuperar no solo el contenido del mensaje, sino también parte de su entonación: no solo hablar, sino también cantar.

noticias.titulo: Russell reactiva la ‘guerra’ con Verstappen: “Va por ahí creyéndose mejor que el resto...”
noticias.resumen: George Russell y Max Verstappen son como el 'perro y el gato'. Siempre se han llevado mal y hace dos años se ensarzaron en un duro cruce de acusaciones que disparó la tensión entre ellos. Parecía que las aguas se habían calmado, pero este sábado en la tercera sesión de entrenamientos libres del Gran Premio de Las Vegas ambos han protagonizado un incidente en pista que ha vuelto a reactivar la guerra.

noticias.titulo: Alonso: "Cuando los rivales van detrás de un motor Honda, dejan espacio extra"
noticias.resumen: Aston Martin ha confirmado en la clasificación del GP de Las Vegas sus peores expectativas. Fernando Alonso ya había anticipado en los días previos que las largas rectas del circuito del Strip iban a ser muy duras para el AMR26 y el motor Honda. Y a la hora de la verdad, los dos coches del equipo han caído eliminados en la Q1 –Alonso decimonoveno y Stroll, vigésimo– , quedándose a más de un segundo del tiempo de corte.

noticias.titulo: Pablo Bustinduy, portavoz de Frente Amplio: "No hay que preocuparse por el impuesto a la herencia de la familia de Amancio Ortega, les va a ir muy bien durante generaciones"
noticias.resumen: Pablo Bustinduy es ministro de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, así como el portavoz de campaña de Frente Amplio en la carrera hacia las generales. Este jueves estuvo en A Coruña, donde tiene orígenes familiares, para participar en actos de una campaña que su formación centra en la vivienda.

noticias.titulo: La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal celebra 80 años con un homenaje a las mujeres del tomate
noticias.texto:
La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal celebra 80 años con un homenaje a las mujeres del tomate
La entidad conmemoró su aniversario en los Llanos de La Higuera con un repaso a su historia y al papel de las trabajadoras de la zafra
La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal ha celebrado su 80 aniversario con un acto en su sede de los Llanos de La Higuera, en Tuineje, en el que repasó su trayectoria y rindió un homenaje especial a las mujeres que trabajaron durante décadas en la zafra del tomate.
El acto contó con la presencia de la presidenta del Cabildo de Fuerteventura, Lola García; el alcalde de Tuineje, David Herrera; el consejero insular de Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca, Enrique Pérez, y la consejera de Promoción Económica, Nuria Cabrera.
La jornada comenzó con una representación de la asociación Acaicate y contó además con la intervención de Marcelo Rodríguez Quintana, director general de la Cooperativa Agrícola de La Aldea de San Nicolás (COAGRISAN), que compartió la experiencia de esa entidad.
Lola García recordó que la cooperativa surgió cuando pequeños agricultores decidieron organizarse para producir y comercializar conjuntamente en Fuerteventura.
"En una época en la que apenas llegaban alimentos a Fuerteventura, la cooperativa ayudó a abastecer a la isla y dio trabajo a muchas familias. Y el tomate majorero salió de aquí y llegó a la Península y a distintos países de Europa", señaló.
La presidenta insular destacó también que "cuando compramos un tomate, una verdura o un queso de Fuerteventura, ayudamos a mantener el empleo en nuestros pueblos y a que perdure una forma de vida que forma parte de nuestra identidad".
La cooperativa nació en 1946 con 34 socios y llegó a agrupar a casi 300 agricultores durante el auge de la producción tomatera
García recordó asimismo a quienes fundaron la entidad en 1946 y a las personas que la han presidido, entre ellas Juan de Saá, que estuvo al frente durante casi tres décadas.
También dedicó parte de su intervención a las mujeres del campo majorero, que "durante muchos años trabajaron el tomate sin recibir el reconocimiento que merecían".
El alcalde de Tuineje, David Herrera, destacó que la cooperativa forma parte de la historia y la identidad del municipio y reconoció el trabajo desarrollado por las familias agricultoras durante sus ocho décadas de actividad.
Por su parte, Enrique Pérez consideró que la trayectoria de la entidad demuestra que "unirse funciona".
"Hace ochenta años un grupo de agricultores entendió que, vendiendo juntos, tenían más fuerza. Esa idea sigue vigente hoy, con el agua, los costes de producción y la doble insularidad como grandes retos", afirmó.
La consejera de Promoción Económica, Nuria Cabrera, definió a la cooperativa como "símbolo de la resiliencia y la lucha del pueblo majorero" y recordó especialmente a las mujeres de la zafra del tomate.
Cabrera las calificó como "heroínas que hicieron de este producto el más exportado de Fuerteventura" y señaló que las administraciones y el sector deben trabajar conjuntamente para recuperar el peso del sector primario en la economía insular.
Ochenta años de actividad
La celebración incluyó una mesa sobre la historia de la cooperativa en la que participaron el técnico Jorge Mesa, Marcelo Rodríguez y dos mujeres vinculadas a la zafra del tomate, Fátima Marrero y Ángela Brito Armas.
El acto incluyó una mesa sobre la trayectoria de la entidad, la experiencia de la cooperativa de La Aldea y una distinción del Cabildo de Fuerteventura
La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal nació en 1946, cuando 34 socios encabezados por Sebastián Ramos Ramos se unieron para defender el trabajo de los agricultores locales y comercializar conjuntamente sus cosechas.
Durante los años sesenta, cuando Tuineje concentraba tres cuartas partes de la producción tomatera de Fuerteventura, la entidad se refundó, incorporó nuevos socios, abrió su propio almacén de empaquetado y comenzó a exportar directamente a Europa bajo la marca de tomates Ramos. En ese periodo llegó a reunir a casi 300 agricultores.
La historia de la cooperativa estuvo ligada también al trabajo de las mujeres de la zafra, tanto en el campo como en los almacenes de empaquetado.
Desde 2022, la entidad desarrolla una nueva etapa desde sus instalaciones de los Llanos de La Higuera, con la recuperación de zonas de empaquetado y vivero y con acciones de formación técnica destinadas a nuevos productores.
El acto de aniversario concluyó con la entrega de una distinción a la cooperativa por parte de la presidenta del Cabildo de Fuerteventura en reconocimiento a sus ocho décadas de actividad.

noticias.titulo: Ligera calima en altura durante el fin de semana
noticias.texto:
Ligera calima en altura durante el fin de semana
Las temperaturas seguirán siendo anormalmente altas para la época del año
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura
La calima volverá este sábado a los cielos de Fuerteventura, que estarán, por lo demás, despejados o prácticamente, en un día de viento flojo que solo arreciará localmente a moderado en algunas latitudes y pocos cambios de temperaturas, según la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología.
La máxima llegará a 26 grados en Puerto del Rosario y podría rozar los 30 en muchos puntos del interior de la isla, la mínima será de 21 grados. Viento flojo con predominio del nordeste, aunque con expectativas de arreciar a moderado y virar a norte en determinadas áreas por la tarde.
En cuanto al estado del mar se espera viento variable con predominio del este y fuerza 1 a 3 con posibles repuntes aislados de 4, mar rizada o marejadilla y mar de fondo del noroeste de 2 a 3 metros, se recomienda precaución al norte y este de la isla

noticias.titulo: Fuerteventura da la bienvenida a las Neurolimpiadas Canarias 2026
noticias.texto:
Fuerteventura da la bienvenida a las Neurolimpiadas Canarias 2026
Amigos de Pájara, Camellito y Las Apañás representan a Fuerteventura en la competición que arrancó con un pasacalle inaugural por las calles de Morro Jable
Fuerteventura es la sede de la gran final de las Neurolimpiadas Canarias 2026, con una competición que reunirá durante todo el fin de semana, en el municipio de Pájara, a personas mayores de toda Canarias.
El evento ha comenzado en la tarde del viernes, 20 de noviembre, con el pasacalle neurolímpico formado por los equipos que desfilaron desde la Avenida de la Constitución hasta la Plaza de Los Pescadores de Morro Jable.
En la ceremonia inaugural, tanto la presidenta del Cabildo de Fuerteventura, Lola García, como el consejero de Acción Social, Víctor Alonso, expresaron el orgullo que supone acoger en la isla majorera la competición final de un proyecto tan necesario para promover el bienestar y el envejecimiento activo de las personas mayores.
Asimismo, desearon suerte a los equipos que se clasificaron el pasado mes de octubre en las Neuromajo y que representarán a Fuerteventura en la final regional de este fin de semana: Amigos de Pájara, Camellito de Tuineje y Las Apañás de Puerto del Rosario. Además, agradecieron a Grupo Barceló que colabora en el hospedaje de las personas participantes en NeuroCanarias 2026.
En el acto, intervino, además, el alcalde de Pájara, Alejandro Jorge, quien resaltó el orgullo que supone la celebración de este tipo de eventos en el municipio, que favorecen el envejecimiento activo, la autonomía personal y la calidad de vida.
Estuvo presente, además, la concejala de Tercera Edad de Pájara, Raquel Acosta, representantes de los seis municipios majoreros, así como del resto de municipios participantes, además de la consejera de Acción Social del Cabildo de La Palma, Ángel Nieves Fernández, y la consejera de Turismo y Empleo del Gobierno de Canarias, Jessica de León.
Competición
Las Neurolimpiadas Canarias son organizadas en Fuerteventura por la Asociación Neurolímpica, con la colaboración del Cabildo de Fuerteventura, el Gobierno de Canarias y el Ayuntamiento de Pájara, además del resto de ayuntamientos participantes y otras entidades.
Alrededor de 500 personas de las diferentes islas competirán durante el fin de semana en el Polideportivo Municipal de Morro Jable. En la mañana de este sábado, 21 de noviembre, se desarrollarán las rondas de clasificación en el Polideportivo Municipal de Morro Jable, mientras que las rondas finales tendrán lugar el domingo, día 22 de noviembre.

noticias.titulo: Canarias propone 1.017 plazas en el procedimiento de oposiciones docentes de 2027
noticias.texto:
Canarias propone 1.017 plazas en el procedimiento de oposiciones docentes de 2027
Esta distribución responde al objetivo de reducir la tasa de interinidad en el sistema educativo público de Canarias
La Consejería de Educación, Formación Profesional, Actividad Física y Deportes del Gobierno de Canarias, dirigida por Poli Suárez, ha trasladado a las organizaciones sindicales una propuesta de convocatoria de 1.017 plazas para las oposiciones docentes de 2027, correspondientes a las ofertas públicas de empleo de 2024 y 2025. El procedimiento abarcará 34 especialidades, de las que treinta corresponden al Cuerpo de Profesores de Enseñanza Secundaria y cuatro al Cuerpo de Profesores Especialistas en Sectores Singulares de Formación Profesional.
La propuesta fue presentada por la Dirección General de Personal y Formación del Profesorado, que coordina Mónica Ramírez, durante una reunión de la Mesa Técnica con los representantes sindicales, como paso previo a la negociación del reparto definitivo de plazas entre las distintas especialidades.
Esta distribución, que deberá concretarse en próximas reuniones de negociación, responde al objetivo de reducir la tasa de interinidad en el sistema educativo público de Canarias y avanzar en la estabilidad de las plantillas docentes, atendiendo a las necesidades estructurales de los centros educativos del archipiélago.
Las pruebas selectivas están previstas para junio de 2027, si bien aquellas especialidades que, por sus características específicas, requieran una organización diferenciada, podrán desarrollar sus pruebas durante 2028.
Especialidades
La propuesta incluye treinta especialidades del Cuerpo de Profesores de Enseñanza Secundaria: Administración de Empresas, Biología y Geología, Economía, Educación Física, Formación y Orientación Laboral, Física y Química, Geografía e Historia, Informática, Inglés, Instalaciones Electrotécnicas, Instalación y Mantenimiento de Equipos Térmicos y de Fluidos, Intervención Sociocomunitaria, Latín, Lengua Castellana y Literatura, Matemáticas, Operaciones y Equipos de Producción Agraria, Organización y Gestión Comercial, Organización y Proyectos de Fabricación Mecánica, Organización y Proyectos de Sistemas Energéticos, Orientación Educativa, Procedimientos de Diagnóstico Clínico y Ortoprotésico, Procedimientos Sanitarios y Asistenciales, Procesos Comerciales, Procesos de Gestión Administrativa, Procesos de Producción Agraria, Procesos Sanitarios, Servicios a la Comunidad, Sistemas Electrotécnicos y Automáticos, Sistemas y Aplicaciones Informáticas y Tecnología.
Por su parte, las cuatro especialidades del Cuerpo de Profesores Especialistas en Sectores Singulares de Formación Profesional son Cocina y Pastelería, Estética, Mantenimiento de Vehículos y Peluquería.
Esta propuesta, acordada entre Consejería y representantes sindicales, garantiza la estabilidad del personal docente interino mayor de 55 años con al menos cinco años de servicio, al detraer previamente de la convocatoria el número de plazas que ocupan las personas que cumplen estos requisitos, de acuerdo con lo establecido en la disposición adicional tercera de la Ley 6/2014, de 25 de julio, Canaria de Educación no Universitaria.

noticias.titulo: Recordando a las mujeres del tomate en Gran Tarajal
noticias.texto:
Recordando a las mujeres del tomate en Gran Tarajal
La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal celebra sus 80 años repasando su historia y su influencia social
La Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal celebró este viernes su 80 aniversario con un acto en su sede de los Llanos de La Higuera (Tuineje), en el que recordó a quienes han escrito su historia, con un homenaje especial a las mujeres que trabajaron el tomate durante décadas. El acto, organizado por la propia cooperativa, contó con la colaboración de la Consejería de Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca del Cabildo de Fuerteventura.
Al acto asistieron la presidenta del Cabildo, Lola García; el alcalde de Tuineje, David Herrera; el consejero de Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca, Enrique Pérez, y la consejera de Promoción Económica, Nuria Cabrera. La velada arrancó con una representación de la asociación Acaicate y la música fue marcando los tiempos del programa, que contó también con la participación de Marcelo Rodríguez Quintana, director general de la cooperativa agrícola de La Aldea de San Nicolás (COAGRISAN), quien compartió con los asistentes la experiencia de una entidad con la que Gran Tarajal comparte historia, retos y raíces tomateras.
La presidenta del Cabildo, Lola García, recordó que la cooperativa nació cuando un grupo de pequeños agricultores, hombres y mujeres, decidió producir y vender juntos en una tierra árida. "En una época en la que apenas llegaban alimentos a Fuerteventura, la cooperativa ayudó a abastecer a la isla y dio trabajo a muchas familias. Y el tomate majorero salió de aquí y llegó a la Península y a distintos países de Europa", señaló.
García destacó también que, "cuando compramos un tomate, una verdura o un queso de Fuerteventura, ayudamos a mantener el empleo en nuestros pueblos y a que perdure una forma de vida que forma parte de nuestra identidad". Reconoció a quienes fundaron la cooperativa en 1946 y a quienes la han presidido, con un recuerdo para Juan de Saá, que estuvo al frente casi tres décadas y a quien este año se rindió homenaje en FEAGA. Y dedicó unas palabras a las mujeres del campo majorero, que "durante muchos años trabajaron el tomate sin recibir el reconocimiento que merecían".
El alcalde de Tuineje, David Herrera, puso en valor un acto que reconoce la trayectoria de la Cooperativa Agrícola de Gran Tarajal y agradeció al Cabildo de Fuerteventura su colaboración para hacerlo posible. Subrayó, además, que la cooperativa forma parte de la historia y de la identidad del municipio, y destacó el trabajo de las familias agricultoras que han sostenido su actividad durante ocho décadas.
Por su parte, Enrique Pérez destacó que la historia de la cooperativa demuestra que "unirse funciona". "Hace ochenta años un grupo de agricultores entendió que, vendiendo juntos, tenían más fuerza. Esa idea sigue vigente hoy, con el agua, los costes de producción y la doble insularidad como grandes retos. Desde la Consejería trabajamos codo con codo con el sector para que el campo majorero siga siendo un medio de vida para las nuevas generaciones", afirmó.
La consejera de Promoción Económica, Nuria Cabrera, definió la cooperativa como "símbolo de la resiliencia y la lucha del pueblo majorero" y recordó una época de prosperidad en la que el producto agrario se convirtió en una de las principales actividades económicas del sur de la isla, con un recuerdo especial para las mujeres de la zafra del tomate, "heroínas que hicieron de este producto el más exportado de Fuerteventura". Cabrera reafirmó además el apoyo económico que seguirá recibiendo el sector primario desde el Cabildo, consciente de "la complicada situación a la que se enfrenta en el contexto internacional actual". "Entre todos, administración y sector, tenemos que recuperar el sector primario y que sea uno de los motores principales de nuestra economía, como lo ha sido históricamente", añadió.
Ochenta años de tomate y cooperación
El acto incluyó una mesa para repasar la trayectoria de la cooperativa, con el técnico Jorge Mesa, Marcelo Rodríguez y dos mujeres de la zafra del tomate, Fátima Marrero y Ángela Brito Armas, en la que se recorrieron las distintas etapas de una entidad que ha sabido adaptarse a cada época.
La cooperativa nació en 1946, cuando 34 socios, liderados por Sebastián Ramos Ramos, se unieron para defender el trabajo de los agricultores locales y dar una salida justa a sus cosechas. En los años 60, con Tuineje concentrando tres cuartas partes de la producción tomatera de la isla, se refundó, sumó nuevos socios, abrió su propio almacén de empaquetado y empezó a exportar directamente a Europa con la marca de tomates Ramos. Llegó a agrupar a casi 300 agricultores.
Detrás de esa historia estuvieron las mujeres de la zafra, que durante décadas trabajaron en el tomate, desde el campo hasta el empaquetado, y sostuvieron buena parte de la actividad que llevó el tomate majorero a los mercados europeos. Su testimonio, presente en la mesa y en el recuerdo del acto, es parte esencial de la memoria de la cooperativa y del papel de la mujer rural en la economía de la isla.
Ocho décadas después sigue activa y adaptándose año tras año. Desde 2022 vive una nueva etapa en los Llanos de La Higuera, con la recuperación de sus zonas de empaquetado y de vivero y con formación técnica para los nuevos productores.
El acto se cerró con la entrega, por parte de la presidenta del Cabildo, de una distinción a la cooperativa con motivo de su aniversario, como gesto de agradecimiento por ocho décadas de trabajo y una foto de familia para el recuerdo.

noticias.titulo: 755.715 euros para la cubierta del polideportivo de Antigua
noticias.texto:
755.715 euros para la cubierta del polideportivo de Antigua
El Ayuntamiento aprueba el expediente de modificación de crédito para la reforma
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura 
El Ayuntamiento de Antigua ha aprobado hoy en pleno extraordinario, por unanimidad, el expediente de modificación de crédito para la reparación del techo del polideportivo municipal, por importe de 755.715 euros.
El alcalde, Juan Cabrera, recuerda que el polideportivo tuvo que cerrarse por motivos de seguridad, ante el deterioro progresivo de la cubierta, un centro que tiene más de 30 años de antigüedad. El alcalde añade que esta obra era muy necesaria, y agradece la rapidez y el trabajo de los técnicos municipales para avanzar en este expediente y acometer esta obra lo antes posible.
El concejal de Deportes, Alejandro García, expone que los informes técnicos de Deportes y Urbanismo recomendaban el cierre y suspender las actividades para evitar la circulación de personas en la zona de riesgo, con el fin de preservar la integridad física de las personas.
El concejal de Urbanismo e Infraestructuras, David Alberto Guerra, recuerda que ya se presentó en una moción en el mes de marzo para solicitar la reforma de la cubierta del pabellón de forma urgente, al anterior alcalde, pero nunca se preocupó por resolver este problema. “Aprobar hoy esta partida nos alegra mucho porque es un centro de referencia para la práctica deportiva, especialmente para la lucha canaria”, insiste David Alberto.
Finalmente, el alcalde, Juan Cabrera, pide disculpas al equipo de lucha CL Unión Antigua, deportistas y aficionados por los problemas que supone el cierre de esta instalación pero “el resultado final y la modernización del pabellón compensará todo el esfuerzo y esperamos poder inaugurarlo pronto”.

noticias.titulo: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
noticias.resumen: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.
noticias.texto:
Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
- Published
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.
In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".
He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.
"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.
The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.
"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."
The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.
This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes by Ukrainian forces destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.
Russian attacks on Ukraine continued on Friday evening and overnight: a seven-year-old boy was killed in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region. Local officials say he had been in a playground at the time.
A 20-year-old female medic was also killed. A local official added that when rescuers rushed to the scene, the same site was targeted again with jet powered drones. Another 58 people were injured in the city.
Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Zelensky was speaking ahead of a meeting in Kyiv with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, who told the Ukrainian president he was here to show that Europe was united in its support.
"The more Putin tries to divide us, the more resolute we become," Streeting said.
He said that Russian missiles hitting Poland on Friday, during military exercises of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, was an "outrageous provocation".
The timing, Streeting said, seemed "more than a coincidence".
Asked by the BBC about Nato's response, he said the best way was to "do more for Ukraine" to defend itself against Putin who he called a "cold-blooded killer".
Streeting's description of Putin chimed with the comments made earlier by Zelensky, who described the Kremlin leader a "killer". This was done in response to US President Donald Trump referring this week to Putin as his "friend".
Streeting's visit to Kyiv came after European leaders meeting in Berlin on Thursday alongside US envoys said they were ready for negotiations with Moscow on ending the war in Ukraine.
"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".
Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president - who had also dialled into the meeting from Air Force One - wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side".
Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks - but earlier this week he invited European representatives to Moscow as it wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".
That meeting in the German capital came hours after Putin had held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China, with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Zelensky said he had been "sceptical" ahead of the latest round of talks, when US envoys claimed that Russia was prepared to make compromises to end the war.
"I thought [Putin] would find reason to escalate."
Speaking to the BBC, Streeting added: "Putin has absolutely no business playing the victim. He is the aggressor in this war. He provoked an illegal invasion of Ukraine. And all of us, right throughout the world, need to judge Putin not on his words, but on his actions."
In a separate development on Saturday, Finland said it "detected a drone strike on a Russian merchant vessel" in the eastern Gulf of Finland, "in an international maritime area".
The Finnish defence ministry said in a statement that the vessel was damaged, without giving any further details.
It added that "temporary restrictions on aviation and maritime areas in the eastern Gulf of Finland" were now reinstated for safety reasons.
Russia has not publicly commented on the issue.

noticias.titulo: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
noticias.resumen: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
noticias.texto:
Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
- Published
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.
The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.
"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."
Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.
The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.
The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.
Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.
This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.
Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".
A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."
The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.
It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.
Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.
Defence Minister Antti HÃ¤kkÃ¤nen said that the Finnish Border Guard were responsible for the investigation into the attack and were co-operating with other relevant authorities.
Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.
The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.
Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

noticias.resumen: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.
noticias.texto:
Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
- Published
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained along with his lieutenant by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.
Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.
Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.
Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using "stealth and surprise", establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
However, they "came under attack from gunfire and explosives" before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores and his second-in-command, it added.
Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.
The two detainees were subsequently flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said.
When he was added to the FBI's most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture.
Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico.
He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.
The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.
Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the BeltrÃ¡n Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.
His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.
Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country's cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.
Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

noticias.resumen: The reported hacking is the latest in ​a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.
noticias.texto:
FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
The reported hacking is the latest in a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.
The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.
President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.
“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.
On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.
The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.
In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.
The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.
In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.
“Maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all these other hoaxes,” he said in an apparent reference to his discontent with the FBI’s investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 US election.
In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber group that claimed it had stolen sensitive information on the bureau’s 38,000 employees.
Additionally, in March, the agency said it had been investigating “suspicious activities” on some of its internal systems, The Associated Press news agency reported.
FBI Director Kash Patel, who has not publicly commented on the most recent hacking, was not present for a Wednesday hearing at the US Capitol to examine threats against the US. Patel’s deputy, Christopher Raia, attended in his place, joining US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

noticias.titulo: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
noticias.resumen: One of sport's biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.
noticias.texto:
Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
One of sport’s biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.
Who: Liverpool vs Manchester United
What: English Premier League
When: Sunday, November 22 , at 4:30pm (16:30 GMT)
Where: Anfield in Liverpool, United Kingdom
How to follow: Al Jazeera will have full text commentary coverage of the game with build-up from 13:30 GMT
The latest rebuild of Manchester United begins at Liverpool on Sunday with Mauricio Pochettino in the hot seat – a position that some see as the impossible job.
The match at Anfield comes four days after the arrival of the Argentinian, who only oversaw his final game as United States coach on Wednesday.
The 54-year-old is tasked with ending a 13-year wait for a 21st Premier League title – only Liverpool have won the competition as many times as the Red Devils.
United sacked Michael Carrick last week with the team third from bottom in the league and suffering their worst league start for 40 years.
Pochettino is the ninth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired with the club’s last league title in 2014 and he is the fourth in the last three years.
United’s recent pain is made worse by Liverpool’s revival in the last decade, with the Reds sitting fourth in the table and hoping to mount a challenge this season to move clear as the team with the most English top-flight titles.
What were the key takeaways from Pochettino’s Man United media conference?
Given the swift turnaround from his previous role to his new one, Pochettino’s unveiling as United manager was combined with the pre-game media briefing ahead of the Anfield trip.
Understandably, most of the questions centred on how United’s form can be reversed in the short and long-term.
“It is about building our own way here,” Pochettino said when asked what he can do differently to the other managers who have taken on the role since Ferguson’s farewell. “The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday.”
“We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority.
“It is normal when you don’t win games that the confidence starts to go down,” he said. “I think the players need to feel from us that we believe and trust in them.
“With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn’t appear for different reasons.”
A key figure in any rebuilding effort will be captain Bruno Fernandes, whose future has been the subject of speculation as he has yet to agree a new deal.
Pochettino revealed he had already held extensive talks with the Portugal midfielder and indicated he remained central to his plans.
“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” he said.
“We spoke, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually. It was very nice contact.”
Questions about the squad’s fitness levels have swirled around Old Trafford, but Pochettino refused to criticise what he had inherited.
“It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field,” he said.
“We cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but we need to be honest, sometimes they don’t show something that you can see on the field.
“We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players.”
What have Liverpool said ahead of Manchester United’s visit?
Liverpool had lost consecutive games before their 3-1 win against bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace in their last match.
The run summed up the mixed start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer – the former Bournemouth manager admits an epic encounter awaits.
“You don’t find bigger games than this, honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.
“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.
“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”
Iraola also admitted he fears Pochettino, whose Premier League experience was gained at Tottenham and Chelsea, will have an advantage because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.
“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” Iraola said.
“We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.
“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”
Iraola will have to adapt on the fly and the Spaniard plans to switch up his game plan if he is caught out by Pochettino’s tactics.
“Especially the beginning of the game will be important as we have to adapt to certain things and manage the situation as quick as possible,” he said.
“Every time there is a new manager you want to impress. It happens everywhere. But we have been focusing more on us, how we can improve.”
What happened the last time Liverpool played Man United?
United were 3-2 winners when the sides met in the Premier League at Old Trafford last season.
Liverpool fought back from two goals down in May, only for Kobbie Mainoo to net the late winner from the edge of the box.
What happened in the corresponding fixture last season?
United were 2-1 winners at Anfield in October last year, with Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire scoring either side of Cody Gakpo’s strike.
When did Liverpool last beat Manchester United?
Liverpool last beat United with a 3-0 win at Old Trafford in the Premier League in September 2024.
Luis Diaz scored twice and Mohamed Salah netted the other in the win for Arne Slot’s side.
When did Liverpool last beat Manchester United at Anfield?
Remarkably, the Reds haven’t beaten their fierce rivals at home since Jurgen Klopp’s side emerged victorious in March 2023.
The result on that occasion was, however, an emphatic 7-0 win for Cody Gakpo, Darwin Nunez and Mohamed Salah all scoring twice, before Roberto Firmino added the seventh.
The two following seasons in the matchup at Anfield resulted in draws.
Prediction
Liverpool have been given a 57.3 percent chance of winning the game by Opta’s supercomputer, while United have only been given a 29.5 percent chance of claiming the spoils.
Head-to-head
This will be their 219th meeting, with United winning 85 of the encounters and Liverpool 72.
The fixture dates back to a 2-1 win for Liverpool in April 1894.
Liverpool team news
Liverpool are boosted by the return of injured trio Jeremie Frimpong, Ryan Gravenberch and Virgil van Dijk, while Dominik Szoboszlai has also been cleared to play.
Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley have returned to training but are not yet available. Hugo Ekitike is still sidelined.
Predicted Liverpool starting lineup
Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak
Manchester United team news
Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire are back in training after knocks, while Lisandro Martinez returns from suspension.
Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford are closing in on comebacks from knocks, but it is thought that the Liverpool match will come too soon.
Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko remain out.
Predicted Manchester United starting lineup
Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Dalot; Tielemans, Mainoo; Diallo, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo

noticias.titulo: Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
noticias.resumen: Leeds come from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to shock Chelsea and climb above their hosts to sixth in Premier League.
noticias.texto:
Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
Leeds come from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to shock Chelsea and climb above their hosts to sixth in Premier League.
Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches.
Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart on Saturday by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.
Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London.
Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment.
Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon.
Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period.
Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman.
Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute.
Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home.
Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front.
Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil.
Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool.
While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager.
Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.
Bournemouth and Tottenham on the rise in Premier League
Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game, and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.
Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign.
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.
Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.
Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half.
Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.
Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday, with the Red Devils second from the bottom of the table.

noticias.titulo: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
noticias.resumen: Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.
noticias.texto:
Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.
A Russian attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih has killed two people and wounded 60 others, according to local officials.
The strikes hit the central Ukrainian city on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while six children were among the injured.
About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s city administration.
Vilkul said on Saturday that Russian forces launched further missiles after emergency workers arrived, hitting rescuers, medical personnel and utility crews.
Footage released by Ukraine’s emergency services appeared to show additional strikes during the rescue operation.
Russian attacks elsewhere in Ukraine killed two people in the southern Zaporizhia region, according to its governor.
Russian authorities also reported six deaths, including a child, from a Ukrainian attack on a residential area in Russian-controlled Luhansk, an eastern Ukrainian region.
The violence followed a separate incident on Friday in which two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a member of NATO, the military alliance linking the United States, Canada and European countries.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident on Friday as a deliberate provocation, questioning its timing alongside military exercises involving European countries preparing for a possible post-war security mission in Ukraine.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte condemned the airspace violation on Saturday and pledged that the alliance would defend Polish territory.
The incidents have unfolded as US President Donald Trump seeks progress in negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv.
Trump said on Friday, following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China, that the Russian leader wanted to end the war diplomatically.
Zelenskyy, however, told reporters in Kyiv on Saturday that he remained less convinced than Washington that Putin was prepared to compromise.
Moscow continues to demand Ukrainian withdrawal from the entire eastern Donbas region, which Kyiv refuses to surrender.
Zelenskyy also reaffirmed Ukraine’s ambition to join NATO, while Washington has discussed offering Kyiv security guarantees resembling the alliance’s collective-defence commitments.
Such guarantees remain under discussion as negotiations continue over how to end the war and protect Ukraine from future attacks.

noticias.titulo: India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
noticias.resumen: Indian Youth Congress issues a seven-day 'ultimatum' to the US technology giant, urging it to lift all restrictions.
noticias.texto:
India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
Youth wing of Congress party issues a seven-day ‘ultimatum’ to the US technology giant, urging it to lift all restrictions.
The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party has staged protests outside Meta offices in three cities, demanding that the United States technology company restore the Instagram accounts of its leaders.
The protests took place in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram, near New Delhi, on Friday and led to clashes with police and security guards, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress on Saturday.
In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building that houses Meta’s offices and clashed with police. In Mumbai, protesters spray-painted slogans on the walls outside, and in Gurugram they held banners reading “restore Youth Congress accounts”.
The party has alleged that on November 19, Meta illegally withheld the Instagram accounts of the youth wing’s president and the party official overseeing the wing on orders from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
In a statement accompanied by videos of the protests, the Congress youth wing said, “If Meta wants to do business in India, it must respect the Indian Constitution, not surrender to arbitrary BJP government orders.”
It had also warned Meta on X that it would “storm your offices across the country and stage protests” unless the accounts were restored.
Manu Jain, who runs the group’s social media, told the Reuters news agency on Saturday that two accounts were restored after Friday’s protests, but thousands of other accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government are still restricted.
The youth wing issued a seven-day “ultimatum” to the technology giant, urging it to lift all “restrictions on opposition voices, journalists and creators”.
It asked how many Indian accounts were withheld on government orders in the past six months, and how many remain blocked. It also asked Meta to explain what it called the automated blocking of posts that mention Congress leader Rahul Gandhi or criticise Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP.
On Saturday, the protesters also posted a video of workers putting up a banner in central Delhi that mocked Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, as “Mark BJPberg” – suggesting that Meta favours Modi’s party.
Meta has yet to issue a statement on the matter.
Police action and BJP response
Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai and detained some protesters, Dainik Jagran English reported.
Pradeep Bhandari, a spokesperson for the ruling BJP, accused the protesters of vandalising Meta’s Hyderabad office and “flaunting it on social media”.
India is Meta’s biggest market by users.
In February, the government ordered platforms to remove unlawful content within three hours of notice, down from 36 hours. The government issued nearly 195,000 blocking orders to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July, the Indian Express reported.
Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025, according to its disclosures. It said most were cases in which it was “obligated to proactively restrict content” under local law.

noticias.titulo: Who is El Chapo Isidro, the alleged cartel boss arrested in Mexico?
noticias.resumen: Mexican forces arrested Chapo Isidro in Sinaloa. He was on the FBI’s most wanted list and faces US drug charges.
noticias.texto:
Who is El Chapo Isidro, the alleged cartel boss arrested in Mexico?
Mexican forces arrested Chapo Isidro in Sinaloa. He was on the FBI’s most wanted list and faces US drug charges.
Mexican special forces have arrested Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an alleged cartel leader known as “Chapo Isidro”, who is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, Mexico’s defence ministry said.
Meza-Flores was detained along with two other men on Friday night in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa.
The arrest comes as US President Donald Trump has been pressing Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to do more to combat drug cartels and said on Friday that Washington was working with Sheinbaum “because the cartels are running Mexico.”
“I told her that,” he said. “And we can’t let the cartels run Mexico. They’re our neighbour.”
Who is Chapo Isidro and what is he accused of?
Despite the similar nickname, Meza-Flores is not related to Joaquin “El Chapo” Guzman, the jailed former leader of the Sinaloa Cartel.
Mexican authorities say Meza-Flores leads the Beltran Leyva criminal organisation and is an ally of the Mayos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. The Mexican Secretariat of National Defence said he was wanted in Mexico on an arrest warrant for organised crime and drug offences and is subject to an extradition order to the United States.
US prosecutors first indicted Meza-Flores in 2012. In a 2019 indictment, they accused him of conspiring to manufacture and distribute cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana for the US market between 2005 and 2019. He also faces a firearms charge.
The FBI added him to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list in February 2025, and the US Department of State offered up to $5m for information leading to his arrest and conviction.
“Known as El Chapo Isidro, he’s accused of spending the last 20 years flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, and other deadly drugs, first as an independent drug trafficker and later as the head of the Meza-Flores cartel,” said then-acting FBI Director Brian Driscoll in announcing his addition to the list.
He also said Meza-Flores and his organisation were accused of kidnapping, extortion, torture and murder.
How was Chapo Isidro arrested?
Mexico’s defence ministry said the operation followed coordination between Mexican and US intelligence agencies and involved special forces from Mexico’s National Guard and army.
Troops used “stealth and surprise” to establish a security perimeter around a house in Guasave and came under attack with gunfire and explosives before entering and arresting three men, the ministry said.
It identified the other two as German N, known as “Serafin”, the group’s alleged second-in-command, and Jose N, who they identified as a financial operator. The three men were flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.
Sinaloa’s public security agency urged residents to stay indoors, avoid the area, and stay off the roads, as federal personnel had been attacked in Guasave.
The defence ministry said roadblocks were reported in four areas of Sinaloa after the arrests and that security forces were sent to reopen roads.
Videos from Guasave showed people fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, as well as cars and petrol stations on fire, The Associated Press news agency reported.
Mexico’s security secretary, Omar Garcia Harfuch, said on Saturday that troops would remain in Sinaloa to protect residents.
“These detentions are an important step toward restoring peace in Sinaloa,” he wrote on X.

noticias.titulo: US midterms 2026: What happens before the new Congress takes office?
noticias.resumen: What happens between the US midterm elections and January, when Democrats take control of Congress?
noticias.texto:
US midterms 2026: What happens before the new Congress takes office?
What happens between the US midterm elections and January, when Democrats take control of Congress?
The United States midterm elections are over, and the Democrats have won control of both houses of Congress. However, they do not take power until January.
Election officials are still certifying results, while the newly elected lawmakers are preparing to take office, and the outgoing Congress is continuing its legislative work.
So what happens between now and January, and what will change as the 120th Congress takes office?
What has happened so far?
After the elections, officials have been finalising the results and completing the certification process, which varies by state.
On November 9, the existing Congress returned to Washington for what is known as the “lame-duck” session.
A lame-duck session occurs when Congress meets after an election but before the new Congress takes office.
This means the Republicans still have the majority in both chambers of Congress and can continue passing legislation until the new Congress takes office in January.
November-December: New lawmakers prepare to take office
During this time, newly elected members start preparing to take office in January.
They attend orientation sessions in Washington, hire staff, and learn more about how Congress operates day-to-day.
Political parties also choose their leaders in the House of Representatives and the Senate. The party controlling each chamber selects the majority leader, while the other party selects the minority leader. The House will also vote on a speaker, who leads the House leadership.
The Republican Party has already re-elected John Thune as its Senate leader, entering the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.
The election on the Democratic side, however, is shaping up to be more of a fight.
Among Democrats, Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Senator and current Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York to be Senate majority leader, with a vote scheduled for December 1.
Speaking on Al Jazeera’s This Is America, Democratic strategist Roger Fisk suggested that the differences between the two candidates may be more about their methods than their political goals.
“I think the difference would probably come in the how rather than the what,” Fisk said.
Republican strategist Doug Heye said the leadership debate reflects wider questions facing both parties after the midterms.
“Both parties have somewhat of an identity crisis,” he said, referring to the Republicans’ losses and the future of the party but also the divisions in the Democratic Party between moderate Democrats and more progressive ones.
December 11: A government funding deadline
One of the biggest challenges of the current Congress is a December 11 deadline to approve government funding.
Congress passed a temporary spending bill, known as a continuing resolution, to keep the federal agencies functioning without approving a full-year budget.
But before the measure expires, Congress must approve another bill to keep the government funded.
If lawmakers do not reach a deal, part of the federal government could face a shutdown.
Speaking to Al Jazeera, Heye suggested a temporary funding extension could push negotiations into February, by which time Democrats will control both chambers.
“So that would probably go through February,” he said, referring to a possible continuing resolution.
Heye also said the federal debt ceiling is another challenge for the new Congress.
“These are two things that never come up on the campaign trail, but it can be very important to tell us about the next two years,” he added.
December 17-18: Congress wraps up
The current Congress is expected to finalise its legislative work before the Christmas holidays.
The House’s final sitting day is planned for December 17 and the Senate’s for December 18.
But lawmakers could remain in Washington longer if major issues remain unresolved.
Even if lawmakers finish their work earlier, the 119th Congress’s term does not officially end until January 3.
January 3, 2027: The new Congress takes power
The 120th Congress starts its term at noon (17:00 GMT) on January 3, 2027.
But January 3 falls on a Sunday, and Congress could pass a law setting a different date for the first meeting.
When the new House convenes, lawmakers must elect a Speaker before being sworn in. Newly elected senators will also take their oaths.
With Democrats controlling both chambers, they will gain authority over congressional committees, legislative priorities and investigations into the administration of President Donald Trump.
“You’re going to have in the House and the Senate something called committee chairs, and they’re all going to be Democrats, and they’re all going to have subpoena power,” Heye told Al Jazeera.
However, he warned that congressional investigations could complicate negotiations between Democrats and the White House.
What changes politically in January?
Trump will remain president after the midterms, but he will face a Congress controlled by Democrats in both chambers.
This means his administration will have to negotiate with the Democrats to pass legislation, while a Democrat-led Senate will control the confirmation process for presidential nominees.
Democrats will also be able to launch congressional investigations and hold hearings looking at the president’s actions and the actions of those in his inner circle and administration.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has already outlined some of the party’s priorities.
“We need to end the war of choice in Iran. We need to stop the Trump tariffs,” he said.
He also called for reversing Medicaid and food assistance cuts and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits.
But Democratic control of Congress does not guarantee those policies will become law. Trump can veto legislation, while overriding a presidential veto requires a two-thirds majority in both chambers.
“I would hope that […] each side would at least be willing to give each other 60 to 90 days to see where they might be able to cobble together a couple wins on behalf of the American people,” Fisk, the Democratic strategist, said.

noticias.titulo: Diallo present as Africa’s Motsepe reiterates support for FIFA’s Infantino
noticias.resumen: Africa's CAF join South America's CONMEBOL in giving unanimous support of FIFA President Gianni Infantino's re-election.
noticias.texto:
Diallo present as Africa’s Motsepe reiterates support for FIFA’s Infantino
Africa’s CAF join South America’s CONMEBOL in giving unanimous support of FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election.
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe has said that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.
Motsepe made the declaration on Saturday in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo, is present.
Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate.
The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat – the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.
CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters, South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL, gave him their “unanimous” backing.
CAF has been consistently behind Infantino – who is seeking a fourth and final term – even after the furore he stirred up in July with his short-lived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Morocco is cohosting the 2030 World Cup.
“Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said.
“I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.”
Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, while CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.
Motsepe, though, has been a vocal supporter, and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.
“You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25m to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.
On Wednesday, UEFA Vice President Laura McAllister told the AFP news agency that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.
“He is a Francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said.
McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice president of UEFA, noted that confederations do not vote as a bloc.
“There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said.
“There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.
“This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe; the same rules apply globally.”

noticias.titulo: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
noticias.resumen: British maritime agency reports two incidents near Oman, while Iran says a tanker caught fire due to naval mine.
noticias.texto:
Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
British maritime agency reports two incidents near Oman, while Iran says a tanker caught fire due to naval mine.
British maritime authorities have reported two incidents involving tankers struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran continues to restrict shipping through the vital waterway.
The incidents were reported on Saturday near Oman, amid a war involving Tehran, Washington and Tel Aviv that began with the United States and Israel attacking Iran in late February.
Tehran has since sought to tighten its control over the strait, which carried nearly a fifth of the world’s crude oil supplies before the conflict.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre, a British agency that monitors threats to commercial shipping, said one tanker was hit at its rear about 20km (13 miles) north of Khasab, a port town on Oman’s northern coast.
Another tanker was struck in its engine room about 31km (20 miles) east of Khasab, the agency said.
No casualties were reported, but it remained unclear whether the two incidents involved separate vessels.
Iran’s navy said on Saturday that an oil tanker had caught fire after striking a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait.
In a statement carried by Iranian state television, the navy accused the vessel of ignoring warnings and travelling with its identification and navigation equipment switched off.
The Iranian account could not be independently verified, and it was unclear whether the burning tanker was involved in either incident reported by UKMTO.
A ‘pattern’
Al Jazeera’s correspondent in Tehran, Resul Serdar, said incidents involving tankers had increased sharply over the past week.
Citing statements issued by Iran’s armed forces, Serdar said about 25 incidents had been reported since the previous Saturday, averaging roughly three a day, a trend he called “quite dramatic”.
“This is becoming a pattern,” Serdar said, explaining that “Iranians are saying the Strait of Hormuz is under their control; that any ship that is passing through the Strait of Hormuz has to be in full coordination with the Iranian authorities and must follow the roads and the lanes that are determined by Iran.”
If ships do not comply, Iran says “they are either going to be attacked, or they are going to hit the sea mines that are laid by the [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] IRGC or the Iranian forces”, Serdar added.
Our correspondent said Tehran was deliberately escalating tensions to send a message that if Iran could not export its oil, other countries would not be able to do so either.
He said Iran was also seeking to show that it remained in control of the strait, a narrow passage connecting the Gulf with international shipping routes.
The US has responded to Iran’s restrictions by blockading Iranian ports and deploying naval vessels to escort tankers through the waterway.
The confrontation has raised concerns over the security of a major route for global energy supplies, with commercial vessels caught in the struggle between Washington and Tehran over access to the strait.

noticias.titulo: Man City claw back 1-1 draw with Fulham to end three-game losing streak
noticias.resumen: Rodrigo Muniz set Fulham on the way but Elliot Anderson volley earns Manchester City a valuable Premier League point.
noticias.texto:
Man City claw back 1-1 draw with Fulham to end three-game losing streak
Rodrigo Muniz set Fulham on the way but Elliot Anderson volley earns Manchester City a valuable Premier League point.
Manchester City avoided the ignominy of a fourth-straight defeat as Elliot Anderson’s strike kept an unsettled Etihad Stadium at bay in a 1-1 draw with Fulham in the Premier League.
Rodrigo Muniz opened the scoring in the 16th minute for the away side, who had only won two of their opening 10 league games to start the day just two points and three places above the relegation zone.
Anderson’s driven volley from the edge of the box in the 57th minute handed City their first point in the league since they opened their campaign with seven consecutive wins.
The midfielder, who had netted his first City goal since arriving from Nottingham Forest, nearly added a second with a burst into the box, but dragged his effort across the face.
City, who sit five points off top spot, had lost to Brighton, RB Leipzig and Forest in their previous games.
Holders and league leaders Arsenal play their game in hand over City at Newcastle later on Saturday.
City held one of the longest winning streaks in English football history with 20 straight victories over Fulham dating back to 2012.
That run is now over, but City’s run of poor results is not.
Boos from the home support greeted the final whistle, with City’s winless run in the league extending to four games — a stretch that has come soon after the club was found guilty of large-scale financial rule-breaking that leaves its future shrouded in uncertainty.
The display was far from convincing for City, with Erling Haaland guilty of wasting two great chances in the first half — and having one goal ruled out in contentious circumstances.
After having a close-range effort saved by Bernd Leno, Haaland followed up and bundled the ball out of the Fulham goalkeeper’s possession and into the net on the goal line.
It was judged that Haaland kicked the ball out of Leno’s hands, with the Premier League saying Leno was deemed to be “in control of the ball”.
